output.brief:
The fall in incidents is not real. The audit trail shows about 37 cases a month still reach confirmed status, in line with the roughly 38 a month before the migration. Forty-seven of them (23 in September, 24 in October) were moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" about 3.5 hours after opening, just before the 4-hour containment limit. The moves were made by a script on a Brackwater analyst jump host that checks every five minutes for cases nearing the limit. The platform connector made no category changes, so this was not a software fault. Those cases then drop out of the containment and SLA figures, which is why Brackwater shows 100% containment and the bonus appears triggered. Only 11 of the 47 have notes describing containment steps, and none has a containment timestamp. I'm fairly sure of this. I haven't established why Brackwater did it, and I haven't checked whether the 28 dropped detection rules also created gaps.

Next steps:
- Do not approve the retainer cut or the 60k bonus.
- Reinstate the 47 cases as incidents.
- Have your own team and Halvard verify containment on each.
- Remove category-write rights from Brackwater's integration role.
- Ask Brackwater for a written account, and review the dropped rules.
